Hi ABC Corp,

We have identified and fixed the issue causing GST to be billed at 12% instead of your configured 18%. The calculation was falling back to a default rate instead of reading your tenant configuration.

data.subject: Extending an auction deadline — PRO-1251
data.body:
Hi Kanti Metals,

You can extend a live auction from Sourcing → Auctions: open the auction, choose Extend on the header, and set the new closing time.

Participants are notified automatically, and the change is recorded on the auction’s audit trail. An auction that has already closed cannot be extended — clone it into a new round instead.

data.title: How is an auction deadline extended?
An auction can be extended until it closes, from the auction header
data.body: A live auction’s closing time can be changed by the buyer who created it, up until the moment it closes. Participants are notified automatically and the extension is recorded on the auction’s audit trail.

data.title: Decision: this needs an answer, not a change
data.body: The customer needs information, not a change. No code, no configuration, no approval gate — I am answering and closing. Waking three agents for this would be theatre.

data.title: Open the auction, choose Extend, and set the new closing time.
data.body: Open the auction from Sourcing → Auctions, choose Extend on the auction header, and set the new closing time. It can be extended any number of times while the auction is still live. Every participant is emailed the new deadline automatically, and the change is recorded on the auction’s audit trail with your name against it. Once an auction has closed it cannot be extended — you would need to clone it into a new round instead.

data.summary: JWT_ISSUER was changed to the API host during deployment.
data.detail: Tokens are minted with issuer auth.acmecloud.com, but the deployed auth service validates against api.acmecloud.com. Every token fails the issuer check, so the service returns 401 for every user on every tenant.
evidence: services/auth/jwt.js:34 — issuer compared strictly against process.env.JWT_ISSUER
Incident INC-382 (January) — identical signature, identical cause

data.title: Fix JWT issuer configuration
data.patch:
--- a/deploy/production.yaml
+++ b/deploy/production.yaml
@@ -18,7 +18,7 @@ services:
   env:
-    JWT_ISSUER: api.acmecloud.com
+    JWT_ISSUER: auth.acmecloud.com

--- a/services/auth/jwt.js
+++ b/services/auth/jwt.js
@@ -32,6 +32,7 @@ export function verifyToken(token) {
+  assertIssuerConfigured(process.env.JWT_ISSUER);
   const claims = decode(token);

data.subject: Authentication issue resolved — ACME-7821
data.body:
Hi XYZ Corp,

We have identified and fixed the authentication issue that was causing 401 errors after our recent deployment. A configuration value for token validation was pointing at the wrong host, so valid tokens were being rejected.

The fix has passed our full authentication regression suite and has been approved for deployment.

Please try logging in again. If you continue to experience any issues, reply to this ticket.

data.body: The deployment manifest sets JWT_ISSUER to api.acmecloud.com. Tokens are minted with issuer auth.acmecloud.com, so every token fails the issuer check and the service returns 401 — correctly, against the wrong expectation.

data.body: Login, logout, token refresh, invalid token, expired token and multi-tenant authentication all pass against the patched branch.

entry.title: Webhook deliveries abandoned when the retry budget is below endpoint latency
entry.symptom: Events stop arriving at a customer endpoint with no error reported to them
entry.rootCause: The per-tenant retry budget was shorter than the endpoint’s p99 response time, so healthy deliveries were abandoned.
entry.resolution: Raise the tenant’s retry budget and alert on the abandon rate. No code change required.

entry.title: Webhook deliveries dropped after a retry budget change
entry.symptom: Downstream systems stop receiving events without any error surfacing to the customer
entry.rootCause: The retry budget was reduced below the p99 downstream latency, so slow endpoints were abandoned.
entry.resolution: Restore the retry budget and alert when the abandon rate crosses 1%.

data.subject: Webhook delivery issue resolved — ACME-7804
data.body:
Hi Northwind Ltd,

Your events were being abandoned because your endpoint’s response time is longer than the retry budget configured on your tenant, so slow-but-successful deliveries were dropped before they completed.

We have raised the budget on your tenant and replayed the deliveries that were abandoned, so nothing is lost. We have also added an alert so this surfaces to us next time instead of to you.

No change to your integration is needed on your side.

data.title: ACME-7804 raised via email
data.body: Our webhook endpoint stopped receiving events for tenant northwind. We are not getting any error, the deliveries just stop.

data.title: Recognised as “Webhook deliveries stopped reaching our endpoint”
data.body: Matched on webhook, deliveries, events, endpoint with 75% confidence. I will confirm it against product context before acting on it.

data.title: Investigation started
data.body: Classified as an integration failure, high priority. Deliveries that stop silently are usually a budget or a threshold rather than a defect, so I want the delivery history before I involve engineering.

data.title: Looking for an agent that can answer product questions
data.body: Asking whoever declares product_knowledge and incident_history in this workspace.

data.title: What does the delivery log say, and what is this tenant’s retry budget?
The retry budget is lower than this endpoint’s p99 response time
data.body: Deliveries are abandoned after the configured retry budget is exhausted. This tenant’s endpoint answers in 4.2s at p99 while the budget allows 3s, so slow-but-healthy deliveries are being dropped. The platform is behaving exactly as configured.

data.title: Decision: configuration fix — engineering is not involved
data.body: The platform behaved as configured — the retry budget is simply below this endpoint’s response time. That is a configuration change on the tenant, not a code change, so engineering stays out of it.

data.title: Stopping for human approval
data.body: Configuration changes to a live environment require human approval. One change, no code, no tests — and the same gate.

data.title: Dana Whitfield approved the fix
data.body: Budget raised and deliveries replayed. Alert added.

data.title: Customer notified — Webhook delivery issue resolved — ACME-7804
data.body: Sent to northwind.ltd@example.com. The reply drafted at the gate has gone out unchanged.

data.title: Ticket closed, and what we learned is kept
data.body: Written to institutional memory as “Webhook deliveries abandoned when the retry budget is below endpoint latency”. The next ticket with this symptom starts from the answer instead of the beginning.
